transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. It's, uh, nice to meet you too. Thanks for seeing me. Um, well, I'm here because... well, I guess I've been having a little trouble at work lately. I'm a construction manager, and, you know, it's a busy job. But lately, I'll start a safety briefing or sit down to review a plan, and I'm really trying hard to pay attention, I promise. But within a few minutes, my mind just sort of wanders off to, like, three other problems on the site. And then I end up missing things that I really, really know I should have caught. It's probably just me being a bit overwhelmed, right? I mean, everyone gets distracted sometimes, don't they? I just want to make sure I'm doing my job right. Does that make sense?
Have you struggled with this kind of difficulty staying focused for most of your life, or is this a relatively new problem for you?

Well, um... I guess it's not exactly a new thing. I mean, I've always been a little... energetic, I suppose? Even way back in, like, elementary school. I hate to admit it, but, um, my teachers were actually already telling my parents back then that I couldn't really stay in my seat. And I guess I talked out of turn a bit. But, you know, a lot of little boys are just restless like that, right? I didn't mean to be disruptive or anything, I promise. 

I also kind of had a bad habit of losing my homework, or... or I'd rush through the directions on assignments before I really understood what they wanted me to do. I always felt terrible when I messed up. I really tried to be a good student, I just had a hard time slowing down. Does... does that help answer your question? I hope I'm giving you the right information.
Do you still find yourself feeling physically restless or having a strong urge to move around when you are in situations where you are expected to sit still, such as during long meetings?

Um, well... I guess I do, yeah. I try really hard to be respectful and just sit there, I really do. But... in those long meetings where everybody else seems to be able to just sit through the whole thing, I'm usually the guy who ends up standing up. 

I'll, um, walk over to grab another coffee, or I'll step outside for just a second to check on something for the crew. I guess I kind of make excuses to move around a bit. I always try to be quiet about it so I don't disrupt anyone! I just get a little, I don't know, antsy if I'm stuck in a chair for too long. I hope that doesn't sound unprofessional. A lot of guys in construction prefer to be on their feet, right? Am I answering that the way you need me to?

In those meetings or even in your personal conversations, do you often find yourself blurting out answers before someone has finished asking you a question, or perhaps interrupting others when they are speaking?

Oh, gosh... um. I really hate to admit this, but... yeah, I guess I do that. I try so hard to be a good listener, I promise. It's just... sometimes when a guy on the crew or someone in a meeting is asking me something, I'll kind of, well, cut them off a little bit? 

But it's really only because my brain is just moving so fast and I think I already know exactly where their question is going. I just want to be helpful and give them the answer right away so we can keep the job moving, you know? But then... I end up answering way too fast, and I'll realize a second later that I completely missed the actual important part of what they hadn't even said yet. 

I always feel terrible when it happens because I know it probably comes across as rude, and I swear I don't mean to be disrespectful at all. I just get a little too eager to fix the problem. Does that make sense? I really hope I'm not making myself sound like a jerk to work with. Am I giving you the right kind of examples?

Looking back at your childhood and your current life, would you say that your difficulties with staying focused and organized are just as frequent and bothersome as your physical restlessness and tendency to interrupt others, or does one of those groups of behaviors cause you more trouble than the other?

Um, well... gosh, that's a tough one to answer. I guess... I guess they both cause me a fair amount of trouble, to be honest. I really wish I could say I had a handle on the focus and organization part, but... um... it's actually been kind of a problem lately. 

I try to keep everything straight at work, I really do, but... well, there have been a few times recently where I, um, missed some follow-ups or maybe didn't coordinate the site quite as well as I should have. It actually got to the point where my boss had to, you know, formally bring it up with me. I felt awful about it. I promise I'm a hard worker, it just... slipped away from me, I guess. 

And, um, it's kind of the same at home, too. My wife... she's wonderful, really patient, but I know she's getting pretty worn down. I'll tell her I'm going to handle something around the house, and I really mean to do it, but then I just... forget. And she has to keep reminding me. I hate being a burden on her like that. 

So, I guess... I guess both sides of it—the moving around and interrupting, and the losing track of things—they both cause me a lot of grief. I hope that's okay to admit. Does that help give you a better picture of what's going on?
